Acknowledgment or part payment - Sections 26, 27 and 28 Limitation Act 1953 - Whether alleged payments between 2007 and 2018 revived limitation period - Whether RM1,000 payment on 11 March 2026 constituted valid part payment - Payment made after expiry of limitation period - Whether payment binds estate under s. 28(5) - Payment by representative appointed under O. 15 r. 6A - Representative not "person liable for the debt" under s. 26(1)(b) - Distinction from Kumpulan Darul Ehsan Bhd v Mastika Lagenda Sdn Bhd [2017] 7 CLJ 525 - Plaintiff's delay inordinate, inexcusable and prejudicial - Acquiescence by accepting ad hoc payments and deferring enforcement Civil Procedure - Originating Summons - Order for sale - Affidavit evidence - Whether Defendant's failure to file affidavit in opposition constitutes admission under Ng Hee Thoong & Anor v Public Bank Bhd [2000] 1 CLJ 503 - judgments.title: JUN JULINA BINTI ZAINUDIN v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Criminal Procedure — Bail — Dangerous Drugs — Applicant charged under section 15(1)(a) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 — Enhanced punishment under section 39C(1) by reason of previous convictions — Whether bailability to be determined by reference to offence provision or applicable punishment provision — Whether section 41B(1)(b) applicable — Held, applicable punishment was enhanced punishment under section 39C(1), carrying imprisonment of five to seven years — Punishment exceeding five years attracted section 41B(1)(b) — Offence therefore unbailable — Applicant not entitled to bail — Judicial precedent — Broad grounds of judgment — Whether binding — Ratio decidendi discernible from broad grounds capable of constituting binding precedent — Court bound by ratio of Court of Appeal decision. Held, dismissing the Applicant’s bail application: The Applicant sought bail after being charged under section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, read with the enhanced punishment under section 39C(1) of the said Act due to her previous convictions. The Applicant contended that the offence was bailable as section 15(1)(a) of the said Act, carried a maximum imprisonment term of two years. The Court held that the applicable punishment was that prescribed under section 39C(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, namely imprisonment of five to seven years, thereby attracting section 41B(1)(b) of the said Act and rendering the offence unbailable. The Court further held that the ratio decidendi in the Court of Appeal’s Broad Grounds in Mohd Faridshah constituted binding precedent. Accordingly, the bail application was dismissed.

judgments.catchwords: (1)(a) when a criminal appeal is lodged by the Public Prosecutor (PP) to the Court of Appeal against a decision of the High Court which concerns more than one accused person (Appeal); (b) one accused person (X) could not be present in the Court of Appeal even though the Court of Appeal has conducted previous mentions and/or case management (CM) for the Appeal; and (c) the co-accused person (Y) is present in the Court of Appeal and the PP has a discretion to proceed with the Appeal against Y only but the PP does not choose to do so - does the Court of Appeal have a discretion to strike out the Appeal pursuant to the second limb of r 105 (to prevent an abuse of process of the Court of Appeal) of the Rules of the Court of Appeal 1994 (RCA)?; and (2) if the Court of Appeal strikes out the Appeal [Court of Appeal’s Decision (Striking Out of Appeal)] - (a) can the PP subsequently apply to the Court of Appeal to reinstate the Appeal under the first limb of r 105 RCA (to prevent injustice) read with r 1A RCA, so as proceed with the Appeal against - (i) Y only; or (ii) X and Y; and (b) in view of the definition of “decision” in s 3 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 (CJA) and s 87(1) CJA, can the PP appeal to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal’s Decision (Striking Out of Appeal)?

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Constitutional Law - Federal Constitution - Articles 5(1), 8(1) and 8(2) Fundamental liberties - Life and personal liberty - Human dignity - Equal protection of the law - Whether it is in violation of medical ethics for medical officer to be participate in the execution of whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.
